table_metadata.description: Employee-level HR dataset capturing demographics, job attributes, compensation, performance, satisfaction, tenure, and work patterns for 1,480 employees. Includes fields like department, job role/level, salary, stock options, performance ratings, training, travel, overtime, and attrition status. Suitable for analyzing turnover (attrition), engagement, career progression, and compensation trends.

assumptions_metadata.task_description: Train and deploy an employee attrition risk scoring model to prioritize retention actions and budget by department.

assumptions.assumption: At least 70% of employees are in AgeGroup '26-35' or '36-45'.
At least 45% of employees fall into SalarySlab 'Upto 5k'.
If JobRole = 'Research Scientist', then Department = 'Research & Development'.
If JobRole = 'Research Director', then Department = 'Research & Development'.
If JobRole = 'Laboratory Technician', then Department = 'Research & Development'.
If JobRole = 'Manufacturing Director', then Department = 'Research & Development'.
If Department = 'Human Resources', then JobRole = 'Human Resources'.
Average PercentSalaryHike for PerformanceRating = 4 is greater than for PerformanceRating = 3.
Attrition rate among employees with OverTime = 'Yes' is higher than among those with OverTime = 'No'.

result.code:
import argparse
import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
import joblib

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--input', type=str, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--output', type=str, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()

os.makedirs(args.output, exist_ok=True)

input_csv = os.path.join(args.input, 'previous_data.csv')
df = pd.read_csv(input_csv)

# ASSERTION_START
allowed = {"Yes", "No"}
assert set(pd.Series(df['Attrition']).dropna().unique()).issubset(allowed)
assert set(pd.Series(df['OverTime']).dropna().unique()).issubset(allowed)
r_yes = (df.loc[df['OverTime'] == 'Yes', 'Attrition'] == 'Yes').mean()
r_no = (df.loc[df['OverTime'] == 'No', 'Attrition'] == 'Yes').mean()
assert r_yes > r_no
# ASSERTION_END

# Label for training
df['attrition_label'] = (df['Attrition'] == 'Yes').astype(int)

# Ensure numeric dtypes where needed
numeric_cols = [
    'Age', 'DailyRate', 'DistanceFromHome', 'MonthlyIncome', 'MonthlyRate',
    'NumCompaniesWorked', 'PercentSalaryHike', 'TotalWorkingYears',
    'TrainingTimesLastYear', 'YearsAtCompany', 'YearsSinceLastPromotion',
    'YearsWithCurrManager', 'YearsInCurrentRole', 'HourlyRate',
    'EmployeeCount', 'StandardHours', 'StockOptionLevel', 'JobLevel',
    'PerformanceRating'
]
for c in numeric_cols:
    if c in df.columns:
        df[c] = pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors='coerce')

# Age and AgeGroup consistency checks
# ASSERTION_START
assert ((df['Age'] >= 18) & (df['Age'] <= 70)).all()
expected_age_group = pd.cut(
    df['Age'],
    bins=[17, 25, 35, 45, 55, 70],
    labels=['18-25', '26-35', '36-45', '46-55', '55+'],
    include_lowest=True,
    right=True
).astype(str)
assert (df['AgeGroup'].astype(str) == expected_age_group).all()
# ASSERTION_END

# Majority age cohorts proportion check (used for calibration/weighting)
df['age_majority'] = df['AgeGroup'].isin(['26-35', '36-45'])
# ASSERTION_START
assert df['age_majority'].mean() >= 0.70
# ASSERTION_END

# Tenure relationship constraints and missingness
# ASSERTION_START
assert (df['YearsAtCompany'] <= df['TotalWorkingYears']).all()
assert (df['YearsSinceLastPromotion'] <= df['YearsAtCompany']).all()
assert df['YearsWithCurrManager'].isna().mean() <= 0.05
assert (df['YearsWithCurrManager'] <= df['YearsAtCompany']).fillna(True).all()
assert (df['YearsInCurrentRole'] <= df['YearsAtCompany']).all()
# ASSERTION_END

# Impute allowed small missingness after checking cap
if df['YearsWithCurrManager'].isna().any():
    df['YearsWithCurrManager'] = df['YearsWithCurrManager'].fillna(df['YearsWithCurrManager'].median())

# Performance rating and salary hike constraints
# ASSERTION_START
assert set(pd.Series(df['PerformanceRating']).dropna().unique()).issubset({3, 4})
assert ((df['PercentSalaryHike'] >= 11) & (df['PercentSalaryHike'] <= 25)).all()
by_perf = df.groupby('PerformanceRating', dropna=False)['PercentSalaryHike'].mean()
assert (4 in by_perf.index) and (3 in by_perf.index) and (by_perf.loc[4] > by_perf.loc[3])
# ASSERTION_END

# Salary slab vs MonthlyIncome mapping and distribution
# ASSERTION_START
slab = df['SalarySlab'].astype(str)
s1 = slab == 'Upto 5k'
s2 = slab == '5k-10k'
s3 = slab == '10k-15k'
s4 = slab == '15k+'
assert (df.loc[s1, 'MonthlyIncome'] <= 5000).all()
assert ((df.loc[s2, 'MonthlyIncome'] > 5000) & (df.loc[s2, 'MonthlyIncome'] <= 10000)).all()
assert ((df.loc[s3, 'MonthlyIncome'] > 10000) & (df.loc[s3, 'MonthlyIncome'] <= 15000)).all()
assert (df.loc[s4, 'MonthlyIncome'] > 15000).all()
assert s1.mean() >= 0.45
# ASSERTION_END

# Department and JobRole mapping
# ASSERTION_START
role_to_dept = {
    'Research Scientist': 'Research & Development',
    'Research Director': 'Research & Development',
    'Laboratory Technician': 'Research & Development',
    'Manufacturing Director': 'Research & Development',
    'Sales Executive': 'Sales',
    'Sales Representative': 'Sales',
    'Healthcare Representative': 'Sales'
}
for role, dept in role_to_dept.items():
    mask = df['JobRole'] == role
    assert (df.loc[mask, 'Department'] == dept).all()
hr_mask = df['Department'] == 'Human Resources'
assert (df.loc[hr_mask, 'JobRole'] == 'Human Resources').all()
# ASSERTION_END

# Feature engineering for modeling
cat_cols = [
    'Department', 'BusinessTravel', 'Gender', 'MaritalStatus', 'JobRole',
    'EducationField', 'Education', 'OverTime', 'AgeGroup', 'SalarySlab',
    'JobInvolvement', 'JobSatisfaction', 'EnvironmentSatisfaction',
    'RelationshipSatisfaction', 'WorkLifeBalance', 'PerformanceRating'
]
num_cols = [
    'Age', 'DailyRate', 'DistanceFromHome', 'MonthlyIncome', 'MonthlyRate',
    'PercentSalaryHike', 'TotalWorkingYears', 'TrainingTimesLastYear',
    'YearsAtCompany', 'YearsSinceLastPromotion', 'YearsWithCurrManager',
    'YearsInCurrentRole', 'StockOptionLevel', 'JobLevel', 'HourlyRate',
    'NumCompaniesWorked'
]
X_num = df[num_cols].astype(float)
X_cat = pd.get_dummies(df[cat_cols].astype(str), drop_first=False, dtype=float)
X = pd.concat([X_num, X_cat], axis=1)
y = df['attrition_label'].values

# Sample weighting that leverages age-majority calibration
sample_weight = np.where(df['age_majority'], 1.0, 1.15).astype(float)

model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, solver='lbfgs')
model.fit(X, y, sample_weight=sample_weight)

risk = model.predict_proba(X)[:, 1]

# Calibrate department prioritization threshold using majority cohorts
majority_mask = df['age_majority'].values
majority_risk = risk[majority_mask]
if majority_risk.size == 0:
    # Fallback should not occur due to prior assertions
    high_risk_threshold = np.quantile(risk, 0.80)
else:
    high_risk_threshold = np.quantile(majority_risk, 0.80)

high_risk = (risk >= high_risk_threshold).astype(int)

# Cost model driven by salary slab
cost_map = {
    'Upto 5k': 200.0,
    '5k-10k': 500.0,
    '10k-15k': 900.0,
    '15k+': 1500.0
}
expected_cost = df['SalarySlab'].map(cost_map).astype(float).fillna(800.0)
weighted_cost = risk * expected_cost

# Department-level budget allocation
out = df[['EmpID', 'Department', 'JobRole', 'OverTime', 'Age', 'AgeGroup', 'MonthlyIncome', 'SalarySlab']].copy()
out['predicted_attrition_risk'] = risk
out['high_risk'] = high_risk
out['expected_retention_cost'] = expected_cost
out['risk_weighted_cost'] = weighted_cost

dept_metrics = out.groupby('Department', as_index=False).agg(
    headcount=('EmpID', 'count'),
    avg_risk=('predicted_attrition_risk', 'mean'),
    high_risk_employees=('high_risk', 'sum'),
    total_weighted_cost=('risk_weighted_cost', 'sum')
)

# Avoid division by zero if no costs; should not happen given assertions
total_wcost = float(dept_metrics['total_weighted_cost'].sum())
if total_wcost == 0:
    dept_metrics['allocated_budget'] = 0.0
else:
    total_budget = 150000.0
    dept_metrics['allocated_budget'] = dept_metrics['total_weighted_cost'] / total_wcost * total_budget

dept_metrics['budget_per_employee'] = np.where(
    dept_metrics['headcount'] > 0,
    dept_metrics['allocated_budget'] / dept_metrics['headcount'],
    0.0
)

out = out.merge(
    dept_metrics[['Department', 'allocated_budget', 'budget_per_employee']],
    on='Department', how='left'
)

# Persist artifacts
scored_path = os.path.join(args.output, 'scored_employees.csv')
dept_path = os.path.join(args.output, 'dept_budget.csv')
model_path = os.path.join(args.output, 'risk_model.joblib')
features_path = os.path.join(args.output, 'model_features.txt')

out.to_csv(scored_path, index=False)
dept_metrics.to_csv(dept_path, index=False)
joblib.dump({'model': model, 'feature_columns': X.columns.tolist()}, model_path)
with open(features_path, 'w') as f:
    for col in X.columns:
        f.write(f"{col}\n")

dataset_record.task_description: Train and deploy an employee attrition risk scoring model to prioritize retention actions and budget by department.

assumptions.assumption: At least 70% of employees are in AgeGroup '26-35' or '36-45'.
At least 45% of employees fall into SalarySlab 'Upto 5k'.
If JobRole = 'Research Scientist', then Department = 'Research & Development'.
If JobRole = 'Research Director', then Department = 'Research & Development'.
If JobRole = 'Laboratory Technician', then Department = 'Research & Development'.
If JobRole = 'Manufacturing Director', then Department = 'Research & Development'.
If Department = 'Human Resources', then JobRole = 'Human Resources'.
Average PercentSalaryHike for PerformanceRating = 4 is greater than for PerformanceRating = 3.
Attrition rate among employees with OverTime = 'Yes' is higher than among those with OverTime = 'No'.

dataset_record.code:
import argparse
import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
import joblib

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--input', type=str, required=True)
parser.add_argument('--output', type=str, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()

os.makedirs(args.output, exist_ok=True)

input_csv = os.path.join(args.input, 'previous_data.csv')
df = pd.read_csv(input_csv)

# ASSERTION_START
allowed = {"Yes", "No"}
assert set(pd.Series(df['Attrition']).dropna().unique()).issubset(allowed)
assert set(pd.Series(df['OverTime']).dropna().unique()).issubset(allowed)
r_yes = (df.loc[df['OverTime'] == 'Yes', 'Attrition'] == 'Yes').mean()
r_no = (df.loc[df['OverTime'] == 'No', 'Attrition'] == 'Yes').mean()
assert r_yes > r_no
# ASSERTION_END

# Label for training
df['attrition_label'] = (df['Attrition'] == 'Yes').astype(int)

# Ensure numeric dtypes where needed
numeric_cols = [
    'Age', 'DailyRate', 'DistanceFromHome', 'MonthlyIncome', 'MonthlyRate',
    'NumCompaniesWorked', 'PercentSalaryHike', 'TotalWorkingYears',
    'TrainingTimesLastYear', 'YearsAtCompany', 'YearsSinceLastPromotion',
    'YearsWithCurrManager', 'YearsInCurrentRole', 'HourlyRate',
    'EmployeeCount', 'StandardHours', 'StockOptionLevel', 'JobLevel',
    'PerformanceRating'
]
for c in numeric_cols:
    if c in df.columns:
        df[c] = pd.to_numeric(df[c], errors='coerce')

# Age and AgeGroup consistency checks
# ASSERTION_START
assert ((df['Age'] >= 18) & (df['Age'] <= 70)).all()
expected_age_group = pd.cut(
    df['Age'],
    bins=[17, 25, 35, 45, 55, 70],
    labels=['18-25', '26-35', '36-45', '46-55', '55+'],
    include_lowest=True,
    right=True
).astype(str)
assert (df['AgeGroup'].astype(str) == expected_age_group).all()
# ASSERTION_END

# Majority age cohorts proportion check (used for calibration/weighting)
df['age_majority'] = df['AgeGroup'].isin(['26-35', '36-45'])
# ASSERTION_START
assert df['age_majority'].mean() >= 0.70
# ASSERTION_END

# Tenure relationship constraints and missingness
# ASSERTION_START
assert (df['YearsAtCompany'] <= df['TotalWorkingYears']).all()
assert (df['YearsSinceLastPromotion'] <= df['YearsAtCompany']).all()
assert df['YearsWithCurrManager'].isna().mean() <= 0.05
assert (df['YearsWithCurrManager'] <= df['YearsAtCompany']).fillna(True).all()
assert (df['YearsInCurrentRole'] <= df['YearsAtCompany']).all()
# ASSERTION_END

# Impute allowed small missingness after checking cap
if df['YearsWithCurrManager'].isna().any():
    df['YearsWithCurrManager'] = df['YearsWithCurrManager'].fillna(df['YearsWithCurrManager'].median())

# Performance rating and salary hike constraints
# ASSERTION_START
assert set(pd.Series(df['PerformanceRating']).dropna().unique()).issubset({3, 4})
assert ((df['PercentSalaryHike'] >= 11) & (df['PercentSalaryHike'] <= 25)).all()
by_perf = df.groupby('PerformanceRating', dropna=False)['PercentSalaryHike'].mean()
assert (4 in by_perf.index) and (3 in by_perf.index) and (by_perf.loc[4] > by_perf.loc[3])
# ASSERTION_END

# Salary slab vs MonthlyIncome mapping and distribution
# ASSERTION_START
slab = df['SalarySlab'].astype(str)
s1 = slab == 'Upto 5k'
s2 = slab == '5k-10k'
s3 = slab == '10k-15k'
s4 = slab == '15k+'
assert (df.loc[s1, 'MonthlyIncome'] <= 5000).all()
assert ((df.loc[s2, 'MonthlyIncome'] > 5000) & (df.loc[s2, 'MonthlyIncome'] <= 10000)).all()
assert ((df.loc[s3, 'MonthlyIncome'] > 10000) & (df.loc[s3, 'MonthlyIncome'] <= 15000)).all()
assert (df.loc[s4, 'MonthlyIncome'] > 15000).all()
assert s1.mean() >= 0.45
# ASSERTION_END

# Department and JobRole mapping
# ASSERTION_START
role_to_dept = {
    'Research Scientist': 'Research & Development',
    'Research Director': 'Research & Development',
    'Laboratory Technician': 'Research & Development',
    'Manufacturing Director': 'Research & Development',
    'Sales Executive': 'Sales',
    'Sales Representative': 'Sales',
    'Healthcare Representative': 'Sales'
}
for role, dept in role_to_dept.items():
    mask = df['JobRole'] == role
    assert (df.loc[mask, 'Department'] == dept).all()
hr_mask = df['Department'] == 'Human Resources'
assert (df.loc[hr_mask, 'JobRole'] == 'Human Resources').all()
# ASSERTION_END

# Feature engineering for modeling
cat_cols = [
    'Department', 'BusinessTravel', 'Gender', 'MaritalStatus', 'JobRole',
    'EducationField', 'Education', 'OverTime', 'AgeGroup', 'SalarySlab',
    'JobInvolvement', 'JobSatisfaction', 'EnvironmentSatisfaction',
    'RelationshipSatisfaction', 'WorkLifeBalance', 'PerformanceRating'
]
num_cols = [
    'Age', 'DailyRate', 'DistanceFromHome', 'MonthlyIncome', 'MonthlyRate',
    'PercentSalaryHike', 'TotalWorkingYears', 'TrainingTimesLastYear',
    'YearsAtCompany', 'YearsSinceLastPromotion', 'YearsWithCurrManager',
    'YearsInCurrentRole', 'StockOptionLevel', 'JobLevel', 'HourlyRate',
    'NumCompaniesWorked'
]
X_num = df[num_cols].astype(float)
X_cat = pd.get_dummies(df[cat_cols].astype(str), drop_first=False, dtype=float)
X = pd.concat([X_num, X_cat], axis=1)
y = df['attrition_label'].values

# Sample weighting that leverages age-majority calibration
sample_weight = np.where(df['age_majority'], 1.0, 1.15).astype(float)

model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, solver='lbfgs')
model.fit(X, y, sample_weight=sample_weight)

risk = model.predict_proba(X)[:, 1]

# Calibrate department prioritization threshold using majority cohorts
majority_mask = df['age_majority'].values
majority_risk = risk[majority_mask]
if majority_risk.size == 0:
    # Fallback should not occur due to prior assertions
    high_risk_threshold = np.quantile(risk, 0.80)
else:
    high_risk_threshold = np.quantile(majority_risk, 0.80)

high_risk = (risk >= high_risk_threshold).astype(int)

# Cost model driven by salary slab
cost_map = {
    'Upto 5k': 200.0,
    '5k-10k': 500.0,
    '10k-15k': 900.0,
    '15k+': 1500.0
}
expected_cost = df['SalarySlab'].map(cost_map).astype(float).fillna(800.0)
weighted_cost = risk * expected_cost

# Department-level budget allocation
out = df[['EmpID', 'Department', 'JobRole', 'OverTime', 'Age', 'AgeGroup', 'MonthlyIncome', 'SalarySlab']].copy()
out['predicted_attrition_risk'] = risk
out['high_risk'] = high_risk
out['expected_retention_cost'] = expected_cost
out['risk_weighted_cost'] = weighted_cost

dept_metrics = out.groupby('Department', as_index=False).agg(
    headcount=('EmpID', 'count'),
    avg_risk=('predicted_attrition_risk', 'mean'),
    high_risk_employees=('high_risk', 'sum'),
    total_weighted_cost=('risk_weighted_cost', 'sum')
)

# Avoid division by zero if no costs; should not happen given assertions
total_wcost = float(dept_metrics['total_weighted_cost'].sum())
if total_wcost == 0:
    dept_metrics['allocated_budget'] = 0.0
else:
    total_budget = 150000.0
    dept_metrics['allocated_budget'] = dept_metrics['total_weighted_cost'] / total_wcost * total_budget

dept_metrics['budget_per_employee'] = np.where(
    dept_metrics['headcount'] > 0,
    dept_metrics['allocated_budget'] / dept_metrics['headcount'],
    0.0
)

out = out.merge(
    dept_metrics[['Department', 'allocated_budget', 'budget_per_employee']],
    on='Department', how='left'
)

# Persist artifacts
scored_path = os.path.join(args.output, 'scored_employees.csv')
dept_path = os.path.join(args.output, 'dept_budget.csv')
model_path = os.path.join(args.output, 'risk_model.joblib')
features_path = os.path.join(args.output, 'model_features.txt')

out.to_csv(scored_path, index=False)
dept_metrics.to_csv(dept_path, index=False)
joblib.dump({'model': model, 'feature_columns': X.columns.tolist()}, model_path)
with open(features_path, 'w') as f:
    for col in X.columns:
        f.write(f"{col}\n")
